title: P36: learned per-head attention temperature (log-parametrized, init 1) on the 078 Muon incumbent
description: P36 (learned attention temperature per head): each of the 5 blocks multiplies its queries by exp(log_temp) with a learned (8,1,1) log_temp initialized to 0, so training starts from exactly 078-claude's function and only 40 parameters are added; the temperature stays in the model through RL and eval. Under 10x decoupled Muon decay the Q/K matrices are held small, which caps attention-logit scale; a decay-free (decay pulls toward temperature 1) per-head scale lets citation lookup sharpen without growing Q/K, which should help expert iteration extend proofs past 6 lines.
hypothesis: Attention logits scale with ||W_q|| ||W_k||. Since 069/070 the Muon matrices carry 10x decoupled decay (per-step shrink 1e-3 at peak LR), and 059-claude showed that capping logit scale (QK-norm with a learned gain that did not grow, max logit ~10) cut round-1 targets and collapsed 9-10 line dev solves, so sharp citation retrieval matters downstream. A per-head log-temperature in AdamW is a cheap, decay-neutral direction for sharpness: the model can raise specific heads' temperature (retrieval heads) or lower it (averaging heads) without spending Q/K norm against the decay, and the frozen RL AdamW (lr 3e-4) can move each log-temperature by up to ~0.7 over its 2400 steps, giving expert iteration a direct knob for re-sharpening attention on longer proofs. If decay is not actually binding on attention sharpness, the temperatures stay near 1 and the result is a tie. Risks: a free sharpness knob could make attention overconfident, reducing sample diversity at T=0.8; and RL AdamW steps on a log-scale are multiplicative on every logit of a head, which may destabilize fine-tuning.
expected_delta: -40 to +40 theorems at >=7 (central guess +5); pretraining steps within 4% of 078's 4782/4706/4711 (a few extra elementwise kernels); final val loss within +-0.004 of 078's 0.0909/0.0918/0.0961; mechanism signature: learned temperatures move off 1 (some head >1.2 or <0.8 in stats.attn_temp on every seed), and round-1 targets solved above 078's 183/145/141 on at least two of three seeds

arch.change: CHANGED vs 078-claude: every block's attention multiplies q (before RoPE; RoPE is a rotation so the order is immaterial) by a learned per-head temperature exp(log_temp), log_temp of shape (8,1,1) per block initialized to 0, so the initial function is exactly the fork Block's; attention logits for head h become exp(log_temp_h) * q.k / sqrt(32). Otherwise 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: blocks are fork Blocks re-classed to TempBlock (subclass overriding attn only) with an extra log_temp parameter; the harness uses the in-process model (as in 059-claude); the fork's strict load_ckpt into a plain GPT would reject the extra keys
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block, unchanged cache code; k and v are cached unscaled, only q carries the temperature. CPU check: cached prefill+decode vs full forward max logit diff 1.1e-6

attn_temp.applied_as: q * exp(log_temp) in bf16 autocast, full and KV-cached paths identical
attn_temp.optimizer: pretraining auxiliary AdamW (lr 1e-3 schedule, wd 0.1 pulls log_temp toward 0, i.e. temperature 1); frozen RL AdamW trains it like any other parameter
attn_temp.persists: yes: TempBlock class and log_temp stay on the returned model through RL and eval

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) on hidden matrices and head.weight; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 078-claude; the auxiliary group gains the 40 log_temp scalars)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: CHANGED: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / 256) per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 2 (070-claude: 1), head (99,256) 1. Every Muon update now has element RMS ~1/16 times lr; only fc2's step doubles.
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases, LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) and the new 5 x (8,1,1) log_temp tensors; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 070-claude (same as 069-claude): fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 070-claude. Unchanged from 078-claude; log_temp tensors are created after all other initialization (no RNG draws) and set to 0.
